newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian city invites ex-king to visit.
newsitem.headline: Romanian city invites ex-king to visit.

text.p: Romania's exiled ex-King Michael has been invited to visit by the mayor of a northeast Romanian city who says he harbours no monarchist beliefs.
"I wrote to King Michael to invite him to come to Iasi at any time he thinks fit," mayor Constantin Simirad told Reuters on Monday from his city, near the former Soviet border.
"I'm not a monarchist, but I'd like to show the King the traces of the past monarchy in our city. It would be a way of redress for the past injustices done in Romania," Simirad said.
Michael, 75, was dethroned and bundled into exile in 1947 by Moscow-backed Communists who seized power in Romania after World War Two.
Officials from his Swiss residence at Versoix had no immediate reaction to the Iasi mayor's invitation to visit.
Hundreds of thousands of well-wishers feted Michael on an emotional Orthodox Easter homecoming in 1992.
Romania's former ruling leftists, who were thrown out of office in presidential and general elections last November, had opposed his subsequent homecoming attempts.
Bucharest had insisted that in order to be allowed to visit, the former monarch should recognise the post-communist constitution of 1991 which defines Romania as a republic.
So far the new ruling centrist coalition, which includes a tiny monarchist group, has not invited the former monarch to visit officially.
